items.readable_text:
Content:
Another way to represent an improper fraction is to write it as a mixed number.

Content:
Let's look at the improper fraction [MATH: \dfrac{7}{5},] shown below.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/98f0536e88c8bbe3156583c11cc7e7f9]

Content:
We can separate this improper fraction into "wholes" and "fractions" like so:

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/989eab0af94696e36f16292186e14589]

Content:
We see that we have [MATH: \color{red}1] whole and a fraction of [MATH: \color{blue}\dfrac 2 5.] Therefore, this picture represents the mixed number

Content:
[MATH: {\color{red}{1}}\,{\color{blue}{\dfrac 2 5}}\,.]

Content:
It's important to realize that [MATH: \dfrac 7 5] and [MATH: 1\,\dfrac 2 5] represent the same number!

Item 8 — Tutorial: Number Line Models for Mixed Numbers

We can represent mixed numbers with number lines.

Content:

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/fb88c92d4c5779868600d0189699d514]

Content:

Content:

Content:
Therefore, the mixed number is [MATH: {\color{red}1}{\color{blue}\dfrac{2}{3}}.]
